extraction.name: NeedleBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive synthetic framework designed to assess retrieval and reasoning performance in bilingual long-context tasks with adaptive context lengths (e.g., 32k, 128k, and beyond). NeedleBench systematically embeds key data points at varying depths to rigorously test models' capabilities in diverse settings. Tasks are categorized into information-sparse scenarios (minimal relevant details embedded within extensive irrelevant text) and information-dense scenarios (Ancestral Trace Challenge, where relevant information is continuously distributed throughout the context).
extraction.creator: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen (Tsinghua University, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is synthetically generated using algorithmic approaches. For information-sparse tasks, needles (key information units) are synthetic, abstract, and fictional statements or relational facts deliberately designed to avoid overlap with real-world knowledge or pretraining data. For the Ancestral Trace Challenge (ATC), data is generated through a systematic algorithmic approach that creates synthetic family relationship datasets with linguistic diversity and logical consistency.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: For information-sparse tasks, the haystack for English tasks is built by extending prompts with passages from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset, and for Chinese tasks, the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset is used. The needles themselves are synthetically generated. For ATC, all data is algorithmically generated.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The ATC generation process includes: (1) randomly sampling n+1 unique names to form a sequential family chain, (2) assigning relationship terms with corresponding generation weights (1 for parent-child, 2 for grandparent-grandchild), (3) generating diverse relationship descriptions using predefined linguistic templates, (4) shuffling all relationship statements to eliminate positional bias, (5) creating question prompts based on the specified question type, and (6) computing ground truth answers according to the constructed family structure.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Token lengths are measured using the GPT-4 tokenizer. To mitigate the risk of instruction truncation, a buffer is subtracted from the target context length when generating each input to ensure that all models are consistently exposed to complete instructions despite differences in tokenizer segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Ground truth answers are algorithmically computed based on the constructed synthetic relationships. For retrieval tasks, predefined core keywords are used. For reasoning tasks, answers are derived from the logical structure of the generated family chains.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For the information-sparse tasks, a keyword-aware variant of the Exact Match (EM) metric is used. For ATC, exact match accuracy is computed based on the model's ability to output the correct answer in the required format \boxed{...}. Manual annotation was performed on approximately 10% of observed errors from the ATC task to identify error types.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 tokenizer for token length measurement
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks. The synthetic nature of the data, while avoiding contamination issues, may not capture all nuances of realistic long-context scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of large language models' long-context retrieval and reasoning capabilities. The benchmark is designed to assess models across varying information densities, from sparse retrieval to dense multi-step reasoning tasks. Not recommended for training purposes as it is specifically designed for evaluation to avoid data contamination.
